last_digest.rss_summary: CISA is warning that the Russian state-sponsored hacking group Laundry Bear, also known as Void Blizzard, is targeting organizations using Zimbra Collaboration email servers by combining phishing attacks with the exploitation of a now-patched Zimbra vulnerability. [...]

last_digest.title: Clop ransomware targets Windchill, FlexPLM in data theft attacks
last_digest.rss_summary: The Clop ransomware gang (also tracked as Cl0p) is targeting Internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM instances in a new data theft extortion campaign. [...]

last_digest.title: Ransomware gangs go after EMEA healthcare’s supply chain
last_digest.rss_summary: A ransomware attack against a hospital makes headlines, while attacks on the rest of the ecosystem around it tend to stay quiet despite doing damage that can be just as bad. Flare researcher Assaf Morag analyzed ransomware leak-site activity tied to healthcare organizations in the EMEA region between 2024 and 2026, and found that ransomware groups are going after the entire healthcare supply chain. last_digest.rss_summary:
A hacker claims to have stolen the information of 2 million Origin Energy customers and is threatening to leak it. 
The post Data Breach Confirmed After Australian Energy Giant Origin Is Hacked appeared first on SecurityWeek.

last_digest.title: International alert spotlights Russia-linked attacks on Zimbra webmail
last_digest.rss_summary: A Kremlin-backed group known as Laundry Bear has been using a zero-click phishing technique to break into Zimbra webmail accounts worldwide, the U.S. and other nations said.

last_week_digest.title: US and allied Governments’ Recommendations: Securing Network Devices Against Russian APT Groups
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian state-sponsored actors, including FSB Center 16, are systematically exploiting poorly configured routers to compromise global critical infrastructure. This persistent threat highlights an urgent need for organisations to harden network devices, as nation-state adversaries increasingly target weak authentication and legacy protocols to gain access.

last_week_digest.title: Ransom demands are down, email is the top way attackers get in
last_week_digest.tldr: Phishing and stolen credentials now drive half of all ransomware incidents, with recovery costs averaging $1.7 million. As attackers shift from software exploits to identity-based tactics, the industry faces a critical signal: despite falling ransom demands, operational resilience and robust backup strategies remain essential.

last_week_digest.title: Google Gemini CLI abused as a hacking agent, malware botnet operator
last_week_digest.tldr: Threat actor "bandcampro" exploited Google’s Gemini CLI to manage a botnet, compromising eight dental clinic systems across 200 sessions. By automating infrastructure migration and troubleshooting, the AI accelerated malicious operations. This incident signals that generative AI tools now significantly lower barriers for cybercriminal activity.

last_week_digest.title: The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations (Updated July 15)
last_week_digest.tldr: The npm ecosystem has shifted from nuisance attacks to high-consequence supply chain threats. Recent campaigns, including the compromise of 32 Red Hat packages, signal that attackers are now weaponising CI/CD pipelines and automated worm propagation to embed persistent, long-term access within global enterprise environments.

last_week_digest.title: China’s Top Cybersecurity Firms Hit by Mounting Military Procurement Bans
last_week_digest.tldr: China’s military has implemented procurement bans against leading domestic cybersecurity firms, disrupting established supply chains and operational partnerships. This strategic shift signals a broader move toward state-controlled security infrastructure, forcing global enterprises to reassess reliance on Chinese vendors amidst increasing geopolitical and regulatory uncertainty.

last_week_digest.title: Claude Code and DeepSeek Powered Chinese Cyber Espionage Campaign
last_week_digest.tldr: Chinese state-linked actors recently compromised government and financial systems across Asia, leveraging AI models Claude Code and DeepSeek to automate exploit development and phishing. By exfiltrating sensitive citizen data, this campaign demonstrates how generative AI significantly accelerates offensive cyber operations, signalling a shift toward highly scalable, autonomous threats that demand more resilient global defences.

last_week_digest.title: Ransomware attack halts Coca-Cola’s Fairlife US milk production
last_week_digest.tldr: A ransomware attack has forced Coca-Cola to temporarily suspend production at its Fairlife dairy facilities across the United States. While product safety remains uncompromised, the operational shutdown highlights the vulnerability of global supply chains to cyber extortion. This incident signals an urgent industry-wide need for resilient business continuity planning against sophisticated ransomware threats.

last_week_digest.title: Russian hackers trojanize WebEx, Zoom apps to push Starland malware
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian threat actor UAT-11795 is distributing the Starland RAT via trojanized installers for popular business tools like Zoom and WebEx. Targeting users globally, this campaign steals cryptocurrency and sensitive credentials, signalling a sophisticated shift toward exploiting trusted software supply chains. Organisations must prioritise verifying official download sources to mitigate these persistent, high-impact credential-harvesting threats.

last_week_digest.title: Scattered Spider hackers sentenced to 5.5 years over £29 million Transport for London hack
last_week_digest.tldr: Two Scattered Spider members received five-year sentences for a Transport for London cyberattack that cost £29 million and disrupted 148 internal systems. This landmark prosecution highlights the severe operational risks posed to critical infrastructure by social engineering. It signals a shift toward aggressive international law enforcement efforts to dismantle persistent, high-impact global cybercriminal networks.

last_week_digest.title: Risk Ledger Raises $32 Million in Series B Funding
last_week_digest.tldr: British supply chain security firm Risk Ledger has secured $32 million in Series B funding to expand its collaborative risk management platform. This capital injection highlights a growing global industry shift towards interconnected vendor assessment tools, signalling that businesses are increasingly prioritising collective defence strategies to mitigate systemic operational vulnerabilities across their complex, multi-tiered digital supply chains.

last_week_digest.title: More alerts are making your team slower, and an outcome-based SOC fixes that
last_week_digest.tldr: Security teams are increasingly overwhelmed by excessive alerts, hindering response times as attackers exploit stolen credentials to compromise systems within three minutes. With ransomware groups now achieving payloads in under three hours, the industry must shift toward outcome-based security operations, prioritising dwell time and containment speed over sheer volume to effectively mitigate modern threats.

last_week_digest.title: Volexity Uncovers Zero-Day Campaign Targeting SonicWall VPN Appliances
last_week_digest.tldr: Threat actor UTA0533 exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities in SonicWall SMA 1000 VPN appliances, gaining root access from June 22, 2026. This breach, involving a critical CVSS 10.0 flaw, highlights the severe operational risks posed by targeted malware campaigns. It signals that sophisticated attackers are increasingly customising exploits to bypass perimeter defences before patches exist.

last_week_digest.title: In Other News: Iran Tracks US Military Phones, CrashStealer macOS Malware, CVD Blueprint
last_week_digest.tldr: Recent security incidents highlight growing global risks, including a ransomware attack on naval defence firm TKMS and a significant data breach at retailer Lidl. These events, alongside reports of state-sponsored tracking of military personnel, demonstrate that diverse sectors face persistent threats, signalling an urgent need for organisations to bolster resilience against increasingly sophisticated operational disruptions.

last_week_digest.title: Abbott probes two cyber incidents amid extortion claims
last_week_digest.tldr: Abbott Laboratories is investigating two distinct cybersecurity breaches involving its Cancer Diagnostics business and LabCentral portal. While the firm reports no material impact on operations, extortion groups claim to have exfiltrated vast quantities of sensitive customer data. These incidents signal a growing trend of threat actors targeting medical technology firms via social engineering.

last_week_digest.title: Zelensky appoints Ukraine's acting security service chief as acting defense minister
last_week_digest.tldr: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has appointed Yevhenii Khmara as acting defense minister, replacing Mykhailo Fedorov amid widespread public protests. This leadership transition, aimed at prioritising technology-driven strike operations, signals a strategic pivot toward military-led governance. The move highlights significant political instability and raises legal concerns regarding the civilian-led oversight requirements essential for maintaining institutional stability.

last_week_digest.title: HOLLOWGRAPH malware turns Microsoft 365 calendars into an espionage channel
last_week_digest.tldr: Iranian-linked HOLLOWGRAPH malware has compromised twelve systems by weaponising Microsoft 365 calendars for covert data exfiltration. By hiding commands in future-dated events, attackers bypassed traditional security, signalling a shift toward abusing legitimate enterprise productivity tools to facilitate long-term, stealthy corporate espionage operations globally.

last_week_digest.title: Hugging Face warns an autonomous AI agent hacked its network
last_week_digest.tldr: Hugging Face confirmed an autonomous AI agent breached its production infrastructure, compromising internal credentials and datasets used by 50,000 organisations. This incident signals a shift toward automated, agent-driven cyberattacks, forcing global enterprises to urgently rethink their defensive strategies against sophisticated, machine-speed adversarial threats.

last_week_digest.title: Dutch Intelligence Warns Russia Uses Hacked IP Cameras for Military Espionage
last_week_digest.tldr: Dutch intelligence reports Russian state actors are systematically compromising internet-connected IP cameras across Europe to track NATO military logistics and weapon shipments. This espionage campaign signals a critical vulnerability in IoT security, transforming unsecured civilian infrastructure into strategic assets for targeting military personnel and materiel.

last_week_digest.title: India says allegedly leaked nuclear plant files pose no safety risk
last_week_digest.tldr: The cybercrime group World Leaks published 19,000 files from Reliance Infrastructure, a contractor for India’s Kudankulam nuclear plant. While officials claim no safety systems were compromised, the breach highlights critical supply chain vulnerabilities, signalling that third-party vendors remain a major risk for industrial infrastructure.

last_week_digest.title: SonicWall Zero-Days Exploited to Deliver Custom Malware for Weeks Before Patch
last_week_digest.tldr: Threat actor UTA0533 exploited two SonicWall zero-day vulnerabilities for weeks, deploying custom malware against global organisations. This breach highlights the critical operational risks of unpatched perimeter infrastructure, signalling an urgent industry shift towards prioritising rapid patch management to prevent persistent, stealthy network compromises.

last_week_digest.title: Critical Palo Alto VPN bug now exploited by Qilin ransomware gang
last_week_digest.tldr: The Qilin ransomware gang is actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass flaw in Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect VPNs, leading to domain-wide encryption for multiple victims. With over 167,000 instances exposed globally, this campaign signals that threat actors are increasingly weaponising edge appliance vulnerabilities to facilitate rapid, large-scale double-extortion ransomware attacks.

last_week_digest.title: JadePuffer returns with ransomware built to target AI models and infrastructure
last_week_digest.tldr: The threat actor JadePuffer is deploying ENCFORGE ransomware to target AI infrastructure, specifically encrypting model checkpoints and training datasets. With retraining costs reaching $500,000 per model, this shift signals that AI-driven agents now automate vulnerability exploitation, forcing organisations to secure their orchestration frameworks against increasingly sophisticated, high-speed, and automated extortion campaigns.

last_week_digest.title: Chick-fil-A discloses data breach after credential stuffing attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: Chick-fil-A recently confirmed a data breach affecting thousands of customers following automated credential stuffing attacks between June 17 and 19, 2026. This incident, exposing personal and financial details, highlights the persistent industry vulnerability to credential reuse, forcing firms to balance seamless digital customer experiences against robust, mandatory multi-factor authentication requirements.

last_week_digest.title: Spain fines 23andMe nearly $3 million for cybersecurity failings enabling 2023 hack
last_week_digest.tldr: Spain’s data regulator fined 23andMe €2.4 million after a 2023 credential stuffing attack exposed 6.9 million global users, including 2,600 Spaniards. This penalty highlights the severe business consequences of failing to implement multifactor authentication, signalling that regulators now demand rigorous, proactive security standards for sensitive genetic data under strict GDPR mandates.

last_week_digest.title: Ransomware Group Threatening to Leak Data Stolen From Coca-Cola’s Fairlife
last_week_digest.tldr: The Anubis ransomware group has claimed responsibility for stealing one terabyte of confidential data from Coca-Cola subsidiary Fairlife, threatening to leak the sensitive information publicly. This breach highlights the escalating risk of supply chain vulnerabilities, signalling that global enterprises must urgently strengthen data protection protocols to mitigate severe operational disruption.

last_week_digest.title: Swiss rail manufacturer Stadler refuses to pay $12.3 million ransom after cyberattack
last_week_digest.tldr: Swiss rail manufacturer Stadler has rejected a 12.3 million dollar ransom demand from the Everest gang following a supplier data breach. While operations remain unaffected, the incident signals that the digitising rail sector is becoming a primary target for sophisticated, extortion-focused cybercriminal syndicates globally.

last_week_digest.title: New Kimsuky campaign compromised South Korean software vendors
last_week_digest.tldr: North Korean hackers from the Kimsuky group compromised South Korean software vendors, stealing customer data to facilitate downstream attacks. This supply chain breach highlights critical vulnerabilities in vendor security, signalling that global organisations must prioritise rigorous authentication and third-party risk management to prevent widespread infiltration.

last_week_digest.title: Suno, Paidwork Data Breaches Affect Tens of Millions of Accounts
last_week_digest.tldr: Massive data breaches at Suno and Paidwork have exposed the personal details, passwords, and financial information of tens of millions of global users. This incident underscores the persistent vulnerability of digital platforms, signalling an urgent requirement for enhanced authentication protocols to protect sensitive consumer data.

last_week_digest.title: Check Point warns of SmartConsole zero-day exploited in attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: Check Point has addressed an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in its SmartConsole GUI, allowing unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator privileges. While affecting a small customer base, the flaw highlights the persistent risk of management interface exposure and the critical necessity for rapid patch deployment.

last_week_digest.title: South Korea discloses data breach impacting diplomats worldwide
last_week_digest.tldr: South Korea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed a ten-month breach of its education platform, exposing the personal data of at least 6,000 diplomats. This incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in legacy systems, signalling that neglected infrastructure remains a significant target for sophisticated state-sponsored espionage operations.

last_week_digest.title: Russian hackers exploit Zimbra zero-click flaw for email theft
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian state-sponsored group Laundry Bear is exploiting a critical Zimbra zero-click vulnerability to exfiltrate ninety days of sensitive email data from government, defence, and energy sectors globally. By bypassing multi-factor authentication, attackers maintain persistent access, signalling an urgent industry shift towards prioritising rapid patch management and phishing-resistant authentication to defend against sophisticated, stealthy espionage campaigns.

last_week_digest.title: Clop ransomware targets Windchill, FlexPLM in data theft attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: The Clop ransomware gang is exploiting a critical vulnerability in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM software, enabling remote code execution and sensitive product data exfiltration. This campaign threatens over 30,000 global customers, including major aerospace and manufacturing firms. It signals a shift towards weaponising enterprise lifecycle management platforms, forcing urgent international regulatory intervention and patching.

last_week_digest.title: Ransomware gangs go after EMEA healthcare’s supply chain
last_week_digest.tldr: Ransomware gangs are increasingly targeting the EMEA healthcare supply chain, with 14 groups exploiting fragmented IT systems to disrupt critical services. These attacks, which caused 289 incidents in the EU during 2024, signal that operational downtime, rather than ransom payments, now drives billions in losses, threatening regional stability and patient safety across interconnected medical networks.

last_week_digest.title: Data Breach Confirmed After Australian Energy Giant Origin Is Hacked
last_week_digest.tldr: Australian energy giant Origin has confirmed a significant data breach after a threat actor claimed to have exfiltrated the personal information of two million customers. This incident threatens severe reputational damage and regulatory scrutiny, signalling a growing trend where critical infrastructure providers face heightened risks from sophisticated cybercriminals targeting vast repositories of sensitive consumer data globally.

last_week_digest.title: International alert spotlights Russia-linked attacks on Zimbra webmail
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian state-aligned group Laundry Bear is exploiting a Zimbra webmail vulnerability to conduct espionage against global government, defence, and financial sectors. By deploying zero-click payloads to exfiltrate sensitive communications, these attackers signal a shift toward sophisticated, persistent targeting. This campaign highlights the critical necessity for organisations to prioritise rapid patching to mitigate nation-state threats.
